items.title: obra / superpowers
items.summary: Superpowers is a software development methodology for coding agents built on composable skills that enforces a workflow of specification, planning, and subagent-driven development. It integrates with various coding harnesses to ensure agents follow red/green TDD, YAGNI, and DRY principles.
items.why_it_matters: It structures autonomous agent workflows to prevent deviation from approved plans and enforces strict engineering practices like TDD and code review.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo and run the quick‑start example to evaluate its fit for your agent stack.

items.title: Google Will Make AI Agents Use Its MCP Servers. The Gmail One Can't Send Email
items.summary: Google announced that from Feb 2027 all AI‑driven tools must access Workspace services via MCP servers, with limited Gmail capabilities.
items.why_it_matters: Introduces a compliance and capability restriction that will affect any production agents interacting with Google Workspace.
items.next_step_detail: Review the MCP API list and plan fallback implementations for missing Gmail actions.

items.title: superdesigndev / treg
items.summary: Treg is an OpenRouter-compatible gateway that provides a curated catalog of thousands of external endpoints and allows teams to register their own tools, skills, and CLIs. It enables agents to call these services via a unified base URL and single token, with authentication injected server-side so callers never hold provider keys.
items.why_it_matters: It removes the need for individual provider signups and custom glue code by allowing agents to access paid services and internal tools through a single interface that relays requests without modeling upstream APIs.
items.next_step_detail: Install with pip and run the example to connect a LangChain agent to a web‑search tool.
items.verification_note: It removes the need for custom glue code

items.title: My AI agents now leave a receipt: an action history for a self-hosted app store
items.summary: The Agentic App Store hub logs every AI tool call as a JSON line to a local file, capturing details like the agent, tool, arguments, and human approval status. This replaces a volatile in-memory status page with a persistent, searchable history that includes rejected or cancelled actions.
items.why_it_matters: It provides a local audit trail for autonomous agents, allowing operators to verify exactly what actions were taken, rejected, or failed, including cases where the AI client timed out before a human decision was made.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo linked in the article and run the sample receipt logger in your own agent project.

items.title: My Simulation Exaggerated the Cost of My Own Safety Feature
items.summary: A simulator bug and an advisory scoring model, rather than the safety checker itself, caused the initial latency and delivery losses in a RAG pipeline. After fixes, the safety layer adds approximately 3 ms per request and maintains delivery rates equivalent to the unsafeguarded version at realistic failure rates.
items.why_it_matters: The safety filter's actual overhead is negligible compared to adjacent components like advisory scoring, which can add 130 ms per request and significantly impact system throughput.
items.next_step_detail: Review the cost analysis to inform your own RAG safety design.

items.title: Building GPT-2 (124M) in PyTorch: weight parity, a speed ladder and about 150 GPU-minutes of my own training
items.summary: The author reproduces GPT-2 124M in PyTorch, verifying weight parity with a max logit difference of 5.3e-05 to 8.4e-05 on an A100. A speed ladder on an NVIDIA L4 achieved 1.48× speedup over the FP32 baseline, while a 60-minute training run from random initialization reduced validation NLL from 11.01 to 4.98.
items.why_it_matters: The implementation provides a verified correctness test for weight imports and a measured performance baseline for specific hardware configurations, though the trained model remains below GPT-2 on HellaSwag benchmarks.
items.next_step_detail: Follow the notebook steps to train a 124M model on a single GPU.

items.title: HF Paper: OS-Omni: Benchmarking Generalist Computer-Using Agents on Long-Horizon Workflows Across Platforms
items.summary: OS-Omni is a live cross-platform benchmark and execution environment that evaluates computer-using agents on long-horizon workflows across Windows, Ubuntu, macOS, iOS, Android, and Web. It provides reproducible initialization, platform-specific adapters, trajectory logging, and executable final-state evaluators for tasks requiring sustained state tracking.
items.why_it_matters: The benchmark reveals that current agents remain far from platform-robust computer use, with the strongest evaluated agent trailing human performance by 8.8 points on average and by more than 25 points on iOS and macOS.
items.next_step_detail: Download the benchmark data and compare against your agent's performance.

items.title: RepoDNA v1.5.4 Released: Browser Storage Reliability and Safer Analysis Restoration
items.summary: RepoDNA v1.5.4 is a maintenance release for an open-source, local-first repository intelligence platform that improves storage consistency, analysis recovery, and release integrity. It introduces atomic IndexedDB operations, accurate recent-analysis ordering, and safer analysis restoration to ensure predictable handling of saved data.
items.why_it_matters: The release ensures developers can revisit previous analyses without unnecessary confusion or unreliable storage behavior by reducing the risk of partially completed storage changes and handling corrupted records.
items.next_step_detail: Check the changelog to see if the fixes address any issues you’ve encountered.
